Sexual Assault Protocol (Adults) 
 
Our Responsibilities 
It is the responsibility of the healthcare provider to timeously attend to survivors and to treat these patients 
with respect and dignity to avoid secondary trauma. Paediatric cases: Please refer to RMMCH protocols 
 
Documentation 
The J88 and a copy of the doctor’s notes are to be filed in the Sexual Assault file available in the medicolegal 
room. If a kit from the medicolegal room is used, fill in the kit number, date of examination, patient hospital 
details and doctor details in the file. 
 
KIT NUMBER 
DATE 
PT NAME/HOSPITAL NUMBER 
DR/SIGNATURE 
 
Consent for examination and forensic collection 
The patient must consent to the examination and forensic evidence collection. They must sign the SAP 308 
form which is usually brought by the police. Spare forms are available in the medicolegal cupboard. 
In the absence of an SAP 308 form, the hospital consent form should be signed to allow the 
healthcare provider to proceed with the forensic examination. 
Offer to have a chaperone (e.g. nurse) present in the room during the examination. 
 
Sexual Assault Evidence Collection Kit (SAECK) 
 
Evidence Collection 
Case ALREADY Opened 
• Use the SAECK with the patient. 
Case YET to be Opened 
• Use the SAECK available in the medicolegal room 
• If not available - phone SAPS to request kit 
• Ensure that the kit register is signed. 

 
* Azithromycin 2g PO stat (if penicillin allergic) 
• HIV PEP starter pack (for 3 days) 
Refer to non-occupational post exposure prophylaxis (NPEP) protocol (TLD 1 tab dly 28/7) 
• STI Prophylaxis Ceftriaxone 250mg IM stat* 
Metronidazole 2g PO stat Azithromycin 1g PO stat 
• Emergency Contraception (4 tabs) 
Ovral/Escapelle 2 tablets PO stat then 2 tablets 12 hrs later 
• Nausea Prophylaxis Metoclopramide 10mg po 8hrly PRN 
Blood results will be checked in Thembalethu and a 28/7 script for ARVs written accordingly. 
Social worker and psychologist referrals on a case-by-case basis. 
Survivor to be given a letter to Thembalethu clinic to collect rest of PEP. 
• 
• 
• 
SAECK kits that are not collected by the police within six (6) months of examination 
may be discarded, as per the recommended protocols 
 
Chain of Evidence 
SAECK to be handed over to the investigating officer. 
Both the J88 and Evidence Collection Forms are to be signed by the Investigating Officer and the doctor 
who completed the forensic examination. 
 
Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) 
Monday-Friday 08h00 to 16h00: 
Patient to collect from pharmacy 
After hours, Weekends and Public holidays: 
Kept in the sexual assault room 
 
 
 
Continuing Care
